references.text: God sends his terror (אֵימָה) before Israel to confuse the enemies and drive them away, a direct parallel to the divine dread (חִתַּת אֱלֹהִים) that fell upon the cities around Jacob.
The nations tremble and fear falls over them when God acts for his people—a clear parallel to the divine dread that protected Jacob's family.
God promises to put fear and dread of Israel over all the lands they travel through, just as He put His fear over the cities around Jacob.
Rahab testifies that fear of Israel has fallen upon all the inhabitants of the land, a parallel to the divine dread in Genesis 35:5.
The fear of the Lord fell upon the cities around Gerar—very similar wording and theme to the divine dread that fell upon the cities around Jacob.
A divine trembling (חֶרְדַּת אֱלֹהִים) fell upon the Philistine camp, a close parallel to חִתַּת אֱלֹהִים in Genesis 35:5.
Thematic parallel: 'those who surround Jacob'—contrast between God's dread that protects (Gen 35) and hostility when comfort is lacking (Lamentations).
